messages:
DeployBot: Alert: autopilot recommends rollback for release v2.4.1 — observed p95 latency 2.6x baseline and 5xx rate +3.2% in canary slice.
alice: @DeployBot can you post metric links and affected routes? :eyes:
DeployBot: metrics: https://telemetry/redwood/canary/4301
DeployBot: affected routes: /embed, /embed/batch
ben: I see the p95 jump on embeddings; this is hitting both hosted canary and a small portion of dedicated test pools. Auto-fallback has paused the rollout at 5% canary.
dave: Oncall — do we trust autopilot to revert? What's the blast radius if we flip back to v2.3.7 manually?
carla: Rolling back hosted canary only won't touch pinned dedicated pools. Routing allows moving slice back to v2.3.7 without downtime. Confirmed with infra.
eva: I'd prefer manual rollback + controlled comms. Avoid auto revert during EMEA change window at 22:00 UTC.
alice: I'll own comms. Draft to send to affected customers:
```
We've detected a regression in embeddings latency after v2.4.1 for a small canary subset. We're rolling that canary back to v2.3.7 while we investigate. No action required for customers using pinned Dedicated capacity. Expected resolution within ~15 minutes.
```
ben: Ops runbook snippet for rollback:
```
# rollback hosted canary to previous release
deployctl rollback --release v2.3.7 --scope=hosted-canary --force
```
dave: +1 on runbook. Carla, can you execute? I'll stay on the bridge for post-checks.
carla: Executing now. Starting traffic shift for hosted canary from 5% -> 0% back to v2.3.7. Will post progress every 2m. :white_check_mark:
DeployBot: Deploy action triggered: rollback started by carla. Job id: dj-rollback-4301. ETA ~8m.
carla: 2m update: ~30% of canary shifted, p95 trending down.
carla: 6m update: rollback complete. Hosted canary now at v2.3.7, p95 back to baseline. Monitoring 30m.
alice: Customer blurb sent to affected list and status page updated. Release notes amended with rollback entry and investigation ticket INV-4301.
dave: Thanks team. Bridge will remain open for 30m for any regressions then close. :thumbsup:
